issues.description: Method Course.addRating(stars:): the template and solution disagree on the return type while the problem statement does not specify one. In the template (Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift) the method is declared as 'func addRating(stars: Int)' with no return value (Void). In the solution (Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift) the method is implemented as 'func addRating(stars: Int) -> Bool' returning a Bool indicating success. The problem statement (problem_statement.md) describes the behavior but does not state a return type. This mismatch leaves students unclear whether they should implement a Bool-returning method or a Void method and may cause compilation or test failures depending on which signature the tests expect.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended signature explicit and consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: standardize on a Bool return to indicate success. Update the problem statement to state 'func addRating(stars:) -> Bool' and that it should return true when a valid rating (1–5) was added and false otherwise. Update the template method signature to 'func addRating(stars: Int) -> Bool' (and provide a default return value if needed). Ensure tests and the solution use the same signature. Alternatively, if a Void method is desired for pedagogy, change the solution to implement a Void addRating(stars:) and update the problem statement to explicitly state no return value.
